analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily 04.11.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 36bps to 7569 (+11% ytd) on a cautious rebound in the AI trade. NeoClouds rose 7% and optical networks 5%. Arista rose 9% and AMD 5% post market on better earnings and strong outlooks.
US 10yr yield rose to 4.95% after a better JOLTS print. Brent is at $103 on Iran deal hopes, Gold at $4009 and Bitcoin at $78k. All eyes are on US NFPs on Friday.
GS derivatives colleagues saw memory hedges unwound and memory/semis upside bought, for example by selling puts.

Midterms: per AP, Democrats won control of the Senate and are on the brink of taking the House. 6 Senate seats and more than a dozen House seats flipped toward Democrats. Congress stays in office through the lame-duck period and new terms begin 3 Jan 2027.

AMD (+5% post market): revenue $13.4bn vs consensus $13.1bn, gross margin in line at 55.9%. GS says results and guidance support its bullish revenue growth outlook through 2027, with very strong Datacenter growth across server CPUs and GPUs. GS expects >80% company revenue growth in 2027 despite PC headwinds.
GS raised its CY26-28 AMD EPS estimates by an average of 11%, mainly on higher revenue assumptions, and lifted the price target from $675 to $700.
Meta raised $15bn in a US$ bond sale that drew $58bn of demand. Its 2056 bond yields around 7.4% p.a.
Revolut cut its AI coding inference costs by 90% over 12 months by making self-hosted models its default.
The Dutch government plans to cut 25k civil service jobs (16%) over 10 years through deregulation and AI. It aims to cut €900m of spending by next year and €3.5bn by 2035.

Norges CEO Tengen hosted NextEra CEO Ketchum on a podcast covering the record-breaking US utility merger, the investment needed for electricity demand, the return of nuclear, and NextEra's preference to build power rather than own data centres.

GS raised its STOXX 600 EPS growth forecasts to 18%/7% for 2026/27 from 15%/5%, on strong Financials and Commodities contributions. Financials are over 30% of EURO STOXX earnings but only 10% of Euro Area economic activity.
Oracle cancelled a $7bn Tencent AI deal under Trump pressure. The five-year lease would have given Tencent access to as many as 100k advanced AI chips across data centres in south-east Asia.
Booking management described travel as mixed, with global demand moderating toward the end of Q3 on international travel, while domestic travel holds up with shorter trips closer to home.

With 60% of S&P 500 companies reported, Q3 2026 EPS growth is tracking at 33% yoy, matching Q2 as the strongest quarter in decades outside post-recession recoveries. The rate of upward revisions has slowed. GS sees AI capex growth peaking.
GS AI adoption tracker: firm adoption rose 0.8% to 24.6% among US establishments, expected to reach 28.6% in 6 months, and is approaching 50% in information, professional and finance sectors.

GS sees limited direct and indirect inflation pressure from the AI buildout, via three channels: higher memory prices passing to consumer prices, spillovers to consumer electronics, and higher electricity prices from data center power demand.
